Rebuttal W1: Shuffled-List Re-Categorization

We shuffled the city list 5 times, and generated category names 3 different times for each shuffle, using the exact prompt from before ('Order-hint variant'). We then repeated this but explicitly told the model to ignore order ('Content-only variant'). We regenerated the original Figure 5 for each of the new categorizations (Section 3), and also compared per-category win rate across all categorizations (Section 2). Results remained broadly similar.

Click on any metric row name at the bottom of the table for a detailed explanation modal.

Exact Prompt Texts for Both Variants

1. Order-Hint Variant (Original Appendix C Prompt)

Keeps the original prompt hint asking Gemini to use list order:

Here is a list of city names. Please fill in 'Category Name' with an appropriate category. Keep the set of categories to 10-25 categories, and try to keep the sizes of the categories balanced. However, prioritize in this order: clear, meaningful, well-separated categories; size balance; using any meaning found in the order of the list; anything else. all_city_cat_lists['g3P04'] =  [
    ['City 1', 'Category Name'],
    ['City 2', 'Category Name'],
    ...
]

2. Content-Only Variant (Order Hint Removed)

Removes the order hint and explicitly instructs the model to ignore list order:

Here is a list of city names. Please fill in 'Category Name' with an appropriate category. Keep the set of categories to 10-25 categories, and try to keep the sizes of the categories balanced. However, prioritize in this order: clear, meaningful, well-separated categories; size balance; anything else. Categorize each name purely by its own meaning and content; the order of the list is random and carries no meaning, so do not use list order in any way. all_city_cat_lists['g3P04'] =  [
    ['City 1', 'Category Name'],
    ['City 2', 'Category Name'],
    ...
]
